headline.headline: WEMBANYAMA'S TURNOVER SEALS KNICKS' STUNNING GAME 2 ROAD WIN
headline.deck: New York takes 2-0 series lead as Spurs star's late miscue proves fatal
headline.body:
SAN ANTONIO — Victor Wembanyama admitted afterward that urgency got the better of him, and in a game decided by a single point, that admission carried the full weight of a 2-0 series deficit. The New York Knicks escaped the AT&T Center with a 105-104 victory Friday night, stealing Game 2 from the San Antonio Spurs on the road and putting themselves in command of the NBA Finals.

Wembanyama, the generational talent whose extraordinary postseason had carried San Antonio this far, committed the critical late turnover that allowed New York to protect its one-point margin. The Knicks, who have now won back-to-back road playoff games against one of the league's most gifted young stars, held on as the final buzzer sealed a result few predicted when this series began. Mitchell Robinson's defensive effort against Wembanyama drew national attention, with head coach Mike Brown crediting an unconventional preparation approach for Robinson's performance.

Charles Barkley, speaking after the game, called it one of the greatest playoff runs in history if New York completes the championship. The Knicks now return home to Madison Square Garden needing two wins in their own building to capture the franchise's first title in more than five decades. Game 3 tips off Sunday.

secondary.headline: STANLEY CUP FINAL SHIFTS TO GAME 3 TONIGHT WITH SERIES STILL ALIVE
secondary.deck: Game 3 tips at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN as the Cup Final intensifies
secondary.body:
The Stanley Cup Final reaches its third game tonight, with both franchises understanding that the balance of the series could tip decisively in the next two nights. Game 3 is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET on ESPN, and the stakes inside the building will be as high as at any point in this playoff run. The series arrives at what coaches around the league traditionally consider the most pivotal game of any best-of-seven.

The hockey world also paused Friday to absorb the death of longtime NHL executive Cliff Fletcher, who passed away at age 90. Fletcher built the Calgary Flames into a Stanley Cup champion in 1989 and later helped reshape the Toronto Maple Leafs organization. His influence on the modern NHL front office cannot be overstated, and the league mourned one of its most consequential architects as the Cup Final continued without pause.

secondary.headline: BAUERS DELIVERS AS BREWERS STUN ROCKIES WITH FOUR-RUN TENTH
secondary.deck: Milwaukee rallies for eight late runs to complete wild 9-7 ten-inning victory
secondary.body:
MILWAUKEE — Jake Bauers drilled a two-run double in a four-run tenth inning Friday, and the Milwaukee Brewers completed one of the wilder comebacks of the early summer by stunning the Colorado Rockies 9-7. The Brewers had trailed entering the late innings before Andrew Vaughn's pinch-hit two-run single ignited the rally that changed the complexion of the game entirely.

The victory required ten innings and eight runs scored after the seventh inning, a performance that will be studied in the National League Central as the Brewers attempt to remain relevant in a division race still taking shape in early June. Vaughn's contribution off the bench proved to be the turning point, giving Milwaukee the momentum it needed before Bauers applied the finishing blow.

secondary.headline: BRONCOS LB COOPER ARRESTED ON DOMESTIC VIOLENCE CHARGE
secondary.deck: Outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper faces criminal mischief accusation with domestic violence enhancement
secondary.body:
Denver Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper was arrested Friday on suspicion of criminal mischief carrying a domestic violence enhancement, a development that immediately cast uncertainty over his standing with the franchise heading into training camp. The Broncos have not yet issued a formal statement addressing the arrest or Cooper's future with the organization.

The arrest arrives during an NFL offseason already crowded with roster movement and contract questions across the league. Commissioner Roger Goodell's personal conduct policy gives the league broad authority to investigate and suspend players arrested on domestic violence charges regardless of the outcome in criminal court, a standard established in the wake of high-profile cases over the past decade. Cooper's situation will be monitored closely as the legal process moves forward.

column.headline: NEW YORK KNICKS ARE TWO WINS AWAY FROM HISTORY — AND THEY KNOW IT
column.body:
Two wins. That is all that separates the New York Knicks from ending the longest championship drought of any franchise in the four major American sports. Friday night in San Antonio, with the outcome hanging on a single possession, New York held. Victor Wembanyama is already the most gifted young player the sport has produced in a generation, and the Knicks just took his best shot twice and survived both times. That is not luck. That is a team that has grown up in the fire of this postseason and refuses to flinch.

Barkley said it plainly: one of the greatest runs in playoff history if they win out. Hard to argue. The Knicks have been tested at every turn, and every turn they have found a way. Madison Square Garden will be loud enough to rattle windows on Seventh Avenue when this series shifts back to New York. Whether the Knicks can hold their nerve when Wembanyama returns angry and desperate is the only remaining question worth asking.

story.headline: GIANTS PUMMEL CUBS 18-3, SCHMITT HOMERS AS SAN FRANCISCO ERUPTS FOR 13 RUNS IN TWO INNINGS
story.deck: Casey Schmitt's 15th home run highlights a lopsided rout at Wrigley Field
story.body:
CHICAGO — The San Francisco Giants turned Wrigley Field into a shooting gallery Friday, blasting the Chicago Cubs 18-3 in a game that was never close and grew uglier by the inning. The Giants struck for six runs in the fourth inning and then added seven more in the sixth, turning a manageable early deficit into a rout that left the Cubs stranded with 20 runners on base and little to show for any of them.

Casey Schmitt slugged his 15th home run of the season to pace a San Francisco attack that also featured long balls from Willy Adames (11th), Matt Chapman (4th), Corbin Carroll lookalike Cox, who hit his first of the year, and Seiya Suzuki, who connected for his ninth. Blake Ray earned the win on the mound, holding Chicago largely in check while his offense did the heavy lifting across a 2-hour, 53-minute affair that included a one-hour delay. Attendance at Wrigley was 39,060.

The defeat was a staggering one for the Cubs, who entered the game at 33-31 in the NL Central but managed only three runs against a Giants club sitting at 26-38. San Francisco's bats produced doubles from Rafael Devers, Luis Arraez, Jung Hoo Lee, and Miguel Amaya, while Lee was also hit by a pitch from reliever John Milner. Chicago now faces the uncomfortable task of regrouping after one of the most lopsided home losses of their season.

story.headline: KNICKS STEAL GAME 2 IN SAN ANTONIO, TAKE COMMANDING 2-0 SERIES LEAD
story.deck: New York survives late Spurs push to win 105-104 on the road
story.body:
SAN ANTONIO — The New York Knicks survived a gut-wrenching finish Friday night at the AT&T Center, holding off the San Antonio Spurs 105-104 to grab a 2-0 stranglehold on the NBA Finals. The win, secured on the road against a Spurs team desperate for a signature moment, sets New York up as the overwhelming favorite heading into Game 3.

The margin came down to a single possession, and it was Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama who provided the defining moment — for the wrong reasons. The 22-year-old phenom committed a critical late turnover that the Knicks converted into the decisive points, and Wembanyama did not hide from the moment afterward. He acknowledged that urgency got the better of him, a rare admission of fallibility from a player who has otherwise been extraordinary throughout these playoffs. Mitchell Robinson, who drew praise from head coach Mike Brown for his defensive preparation — Brown noting with a grin that country music had played some unusual role in Robinson's film study routine — made Wembanyama's night miserable at key stretches near the basket.

Charles Barkley, speaking on the broadcast afterward, called it one of the greatest playoff runs in NBA history if the Knicks finish the job, a sentiment that carries real weight given New York's journey through the bracket. The Knicks have now won consecutive road games to open the Finals, a feat that speaks to the toughness of a roster built around grit and defensive resolve. Game 3 shifts to Madison Square Garden, where New York will look to push San Antonio to the brink in front of what promises to be a deafening crowd.

story.headline: FLETCHER DIES AT 90; GAME 3 LOOMS TONIGHT AS MATTHEWS PLEDGES LOYALTY TO TORONTO
story.deck: Hockey mourns a builder while the Cup Final resumes and Montreal's stars earn hardware.
story.body:
Cliff Fletcher, the Hall of Fame executive who assembled the 1989 Calgary Flames into a Stanley Cup champion and spent decades reshaping franchises across the NHL, died Saturday at the age of 90. Fletcher's fingerprints touched nearly every corner of professional hockey, from his early years building the Flames into a powerhouse through his long tenure in Toronto, where he twice served as general manager of the Maple Leafs. Commissioner Gary Bettman called Fletcher "one of the true architects of the modern NHL," and tributes poured in from former players and executives who credited the Montreal native with giving them their first opportunities in the game.

On the ice, attention turns to tonight's Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final, with puck drop set for 8 p.m. ET on ESPN and the ESPN App. The series is tied 1-1 heading into the pivotal middle game, and whichever team emerges with the win will hold a commanding position as the series shifts home ice. Meanwhile, Maple Leafs general manager John Chayka moved to tamp down trade speculation surrounding captain Auston Matthews, telling reporters Saturday that the franchise center remains committed to winning a championship in Toronto. "Auston wants to be the guy who brings a Cup to this city," Chayka said. "That hasn't changed."

In individual honors announced by the league, Montreal Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki claimed the Frank J. Selke Trophy as the NHL's best defensive forward in a runaway vote, recognized for his elite play on both ends of the ice throughout the regular season. Teammate Cole Caufield earned the Lady Byng Trophy, awarded annually for sportsmanship and gentlemanly conduct combined with high performance, giving the Canadiens a memorable awards haul. The third annual Stanley Pup special, a fan-favorite program spotlighting hockey's most beloved canine companions, premieres Monday at 8 p.m. ET in Canada and 9:30 p.m. ET in the United States.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL OFFSEASON RESHAPES THE LANDSCAPE
story.deck: Big-name signal-callers find new homes as rosters transform across the league.
story.body:
The 2026 NFL offseason has delivered a wave of quarterback movement rarely seen in a single calendar spring, with teams scrambling to secure their franchise cornerstones before training camps open in late July. The Las Vegas Raiders completed the most stunning move of the period, landing former Green Bay starter Jordan Love on a restructured deal after Love requested a trade following a difficult 2025 campaign. Raiders general manager Tom Telesco called Love the foundational piece of a full rebuild, and the team promptly released veteran backup Gardner Minshew to clear salary space.

The draft class has drawn equally intense scrutiny following April's selection meeting in Green Bay. Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders, selected in the first round by the New York Giants, reported for rookie minicamp last week and drew immediate praise from offensive coordinator Mike Kafka for his pre-snap reads and command of the huddle. Meanwhile, the Chicago Bears used their second first-round pick to shore up the offensive line, grabbing Tennessee tackle Miles Alderman, giving young starter Caleb Williams the protection his development demands.

On the free agency front, wide receiver Davante Adams finalized a two-year contract with the Dallas Cowboys, reuniting him with coordinator Brian Schottenheimer in what league observers called a calculated move to extend Dallas's championship window. The Cowboys also retained pass rusher Micah Parsons on a record-breaking extension worth $34 million annually, ensuring their defensive identity remains intact heading into a season the organization believes could end with a Super Bowl run.
